parole.testo: Unknown. The word implies a Vulgar Latin *arganāx. Possibly related to Galician argana, árgoma and argueiro, which would make it a word of Paleo-Hispanic origin.

From Vulgar Latin *barrum (“clay, mud”), from Paleo-Hispanic, possibly Celtic; compare Middle Irish broch (“waste, dregs”) and Gaulish *barros (“the bushy end”). Cognate with Galician, Mirandese, and Spanish barro, Asturian barru.

From Old Galician-Portuguese colmẽa, inherited from Vulgar Latin *colmēna, from Paleo-Hispanic, most likely from Proto-Celtic *kolmēnā, derived from *kŏlmos (“straw”). Compare Galician colmea and Spanish colmena.

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese sẽara, from Iberian Vulgar Latin senara, from Paleo-Hispanic, ultimately from Proto-Celtic *senara (“piece of land cultivated on the side”), from *sen- (“separation”) (< Proto-Indo-European *swé (“self”)) + *aryeti (“to plow”). Cognate with Galician seara, senr
